propositions: The (inbound, probe) dispatch chain has no live producer because differ._compute_mutations_emit_absent_partner_probes only emits when it sees a jira_key in local_state entries, but run_differs passes a fetched Jira snapshot whose entries carry no jira_key field.

The deletion-vs-aged-out discrimination that ADR 0028 §2 requires is already implemented and live twice via outbound_differ._safe_get_issue and binding_walk bounded-GET probe logic, not through the dead inbound chain.

A confirmed hard-deleted issue whose local ticket still exists is currently resurrected by the eventual-retirement path (3 confirmed-404s retire the binding, making the ticket unbound, triggering outbound CREATE), but the same-pass resurrection implementation (via inbound-probe→inbound-delete→_apply_inbound_delete→create_after_hard_delete) is dead in production.

A guard must prevent resurrection of deliberately-deleted work: when a local ticket's binding is retired (confirmed 404 on Jira), outbound-create must be suppressed and the suppression must be observable and reversible via BindingStore.unretire.

The dead producer, dispatch arm route_inbound_probe, and resurrection implementation (_apply_inbound_delete, _apply_inbound_probe, create_after_hard_delete, _build_hard_delete_recreate, pending_hard_delete_creates) must be removed; the absence-probe port capability (probe_remote, SupportsAbsenceProbe, inbound_probe.py) stays dormant with a follow-up.
